title: Telegram to Sun Yat-sen, Swatow to Tokyo, 3 April 1916 (JACAR B03050738800)

steps.what: Syllable statistics: Yamada's 20 consonants, rare u pointing to a vowel-major table.
Brute force of the systematic condenser family scored by a Chinese character LM; winner 49 points clear.
Four doubtful codes fixed by sense and confirmed in the handwriting; content matches Mo Qingyu's March 1916 rising.
Tail checked on a 600 dpi render: the garble is the operator's; three characters unrecoverable.

Tail re-examined as a Morse transmission slip (the received sheet is clean, so the errors are the telegraph's): p (.--.) = a (.-) + n (-.) with the letter space lost, so ropezpo = ro pe za no = 返港 'returns to Hong Kong'. A Morse re-division search (morse_tail.py) of zpo gives four valid codes at one space change (港, 砉, 彼, 嫗); only 港 fits. The last word ngobunibai gives no sensible decoding with up to four space changes; 翼□ (5068) one-letter and one-element Morse slips give no word or known name.

outcome.method_basis: The condenser table (20 consonants rotated to start at l, vowels e a i o u, numbered column-major) was deduced from the ciphertext by analogy with Yamada's known tables, then read through the standard Chinese telegraph code; Tomokiyo's attempts with Yamada's own tables had failed.
outcome.notes: 42 of about 44 characters (港 restored from a Morse slip, M, 30 Sept 2026); the last word, about two codes, is garbled in the received copy; 翼□ second character unresolved.

prior.where: Tomokiyo's attempts with the Yamada tables negative (blog 12 Dec 2021)
